title_as_printed: Mapping grey matter and cortical thickness alterations associated with subjective cognitive decline and mild cognitive impairment among rural-dwelling older adults in China: A population-based study

Task_Type.reason: VBM/SBM group comparisons and logistic-regression odds ratios of regional GMV and cortical thickness with MCI/SCD; no discrimination figure.
Task_Type.quote: We used binary logistic regression models to examine the associations of MCI with regional GMV and cortical thickness.

Category.reason: Structural 3T MRI (grey matter volume, cortical thickness) is the analysed data domain; the population cohort supplies diagnosis and covariates.

Validation_Type.reason: Cross-sectional association study; no predictive model validated.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 1178 is the number who underwent MRI in the sub-study; 106 were excluded (74 poor image quality, 26 dementia, 6 missing AD8), leaving 1072 analysed. The registry uses the pre-exclusion figure without saying so; the analysed N is 1072.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: From August 2018 to November 2020, a subsample of 1178 individuals undertook structural brain MRI scans in Southwestern Lu Hospital. Of these, 106 persons were excluded due to suboptimal image quality (n = 74), dementia (n = 26), or missing information on the self-rated Ascertain Dementia 8-item Questionnaire (AD8) (n = 6), leaving 1072 participants for the current analysis.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: MIND-China MRI sub-study; no ADNI data.

notes: No field in error. Recommend Sample_N_Approx = 1072: the 1178 figure includes 26 people with dementia and 74 unusable scans excluded from every analysis. The paper's own Results contain a typo ('Of the 1702 participants'); the abstract, participant text and Table 1 all give 1072.
